::: {#rem-approximation-limits}

#### What universal approximation leaves out

@thm-universal-approximation says that some network of one [hidden layer](#def-hidden-layer) comes within $\epsilon$ of $f$.
It does not say how wide that network must be,
a [width](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/neural-nets.html#def-width) that can grow very fast with the number of inputs $\inputdim$,
nor that training finds its [parameters](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-parameter),
nor that it predicts new data well
[@goodfellow2016deep, section 6.4.1].

[Depth](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/neural-nets.html#def-depth) helps with the first of these.
A [ReLU](#def-relu) network's graph is made of straight pieces,
as @sol-relu-bends showed for one input.
For networks with the same total number of [unit](#def-unit)s,
the number of pieces a deep network can make grows exponentially with its number of layers,
while a network with one hidden layer makes far fewer [@montufar2014linear].
Some functions with many pieces therefore need far fewer [unit](#def-unit)s
in a network with several layers.

:::
